newsitem.title: UK: Computer games can lift immune system - scientist.
newsitem.headline: Computer games can lift immune system - scientist.

text.p: Experiments show playing computer games can briefly lift your immune system, a leading researcher said on Monday.

Laboratory tests on volunteers asked to perform complex mental arithmetic or test their skills in computer games showed their immune systems were briefly "up-regulated", Doctor Phil Evans told Britain's largest annual science festival.
But Evans, studing how the immune system reacts to the challenges of everyday life and fights off disease, said the effect was short-lived, lasting only minutes.

"The immune system is constantly fluctuating... it is constantly going up and down and what it is trying to do is maintain a balance," Evans told a news conference at the British Association festival in this central English city.

"It would be premature to say we know what every regulation upwards or downwards means... But it is important to put a brake on people who say that stress constantly down-regulates the system," he said.

Evans, who said he used "up-regulates" rather than "boosts" to avoid giving a misleading impression of the effect of challenges like computer games, said the discovery could eventually help explain the link between stress and illness.

Instead of the common belief that major events like divorce or bereavement depress the immune system, Evans said the effect of such major crises could be to damage the immune system's ability to regulate itself both upwards and downwards.
But he said research was still preliminary. "We don't know much about it, what is exciting is that in some circumstances (the immune system) does actually have an upward regulation."
